title: The War Elephants of Chess
body: Long ago, the chess piece we call the bishop was actually a mighty war elephant. A medieval book explains that these giant beasts leaped diagonally across the board because they were too powerful for anyone to face head-on.

variants.lucy: If we could look at a very old book, we would discover that the quiet bishop on your board used to be a magnificent war elephant. These grand animals walked along the diagonal paths of the kingdom rather than straight ahead. It was a gentle way to travel because no one could stand against their immense power in a direct fight.
variants.luca: Picture a giant war elephant charging right into the action where your bishop now stands! Hundreds of years ago, a writer explained that these beasts were too powerful for anyone to fight face-to-face. That is why they leaped diagonally across the board, launching clever sideways attacks that nobody could block!
variants.cn: 要是我们能翻开一本特别古老的书，就会发现：你棋盘上那枚安安静静的象，从前竟是一头威风凛凛的战象！这些大家伙在王国里走的是斜斜的路线，而不是一直往前冲。这样走其实很温柔——因为真要面对面打起来，谁也扛不住它们那股巨大的力气呀。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón
